messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate and queue length on dedicated pool d-nyc-3 since 14:02 UTC. Avg latency ↑ ~2.3x. Paging on-call.
Sarah O: ack, taking lead. linking graphs: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/nyc3/pool-d-nyc-3
Mike R: quick ask — what's the autoscale config for that pool rn? min/max?
Jin M: looks like min=5 max=20, cooldown=10m. pool is at max_instances=20 but we still have large request backlog. GPU mem pressure & KV cache growth. Autoscaler isn't kicking because of cooldown + previous flapping.
Devin (SRE): I can enable burst capacity for d-nyc-3 which allows temporary headroom above max. Options: enable burst_mode (allow +X instances for Y minutes) or raise max_instances. Propose: set max=60 and enable burst_mode for safety. Thoughts?
Emily C: if we raise capacity we should also throttle noisy tenants. Top offender is org-42 — sending big batched embeddings and streaming requests. We should reduce their concurrency and QPS now.
Sarah O: agree. Devin, if you can apply the pool change I’ll coordinate support comms. Mike, Jin — any other quick mitigations?
Mike R: temporarily disable streaming_response feature on that pool to avoid long-lived connections consuming slots. Also reduce batch sizes for inference for a few minutes via config override.
Jin M: good call. We'll also block the problematic model-variant 'large-sparse-v2' for this pool if needed.
Devin (SRE): executing mitigation now — running infractl command:

```
redwoodctl pools update d-nyc-3 --autoscale-max 60 --burst-mode enable --burst-duration 15m --cooldown 60s
```

Devin (SRE): applied. autoscale.max=60 burst_mode=enabled burst_duration=15m cooldown=60s. Requesting extra instances from cloud.
incident-bot: system: scaling action detected — desired +8 instances, 6 launched, 2 pending.
Mike R: disabling streaming feature on pool:

```
redwoodctl pool-feature-toggle d-nyc-3 --feature streaming_response --state off --reason "mitigation: reduce long-lived connections"
```

Mike R: feature toggled off.
Emily C: submitting support tickets and temporary quota changes for noisy tenants:
- SUP-9831 -> org-42: concurrency 4 -> 1, qps 200 -> 50 (temp)
- SUP-9832 -> org-17: qps 150 -> 75 (temp)

Emily C: DMed sales/AMs for both orgs to let them know it's a temporary throttle while we stabilize.
Jin M: monitoring metrics — error rate falling: 5xx from 7.2% -> 1.8% over last 10m; queue length decreasing. KV cache still warm but expected to evict as new capacity comes up.
Sarah O: good. Handoff plan — I’ll hand to night oncall @Jin at 18:00 UTC. Jin, please watch for any re-flare and be ready to revert burst_mode or disable 'large-sparse-v2' as needed.
Devin (SRE): note for rollback and post-incident: add autoscale policy tweak to avoid cooldown blocking scale-ups — proposal: dynamic cooldown based on recent scale events and allow automated burst up to 50% above max for 10 minutes. Creating follow-up PLAT-1422.
Mike R: also note: if errors spike again, use quick command to evict KV cache for offending models:

```
redwoodctl pool-cache invalidate d-nyc-3 --model large-sparse-v2 --force
```

Emily C: updating customer messages. I’ll also add a line to status.redwood.com explaining we throttled heavy tenants to protect overall availability.
support-bot: Created tickets SUP-9831 and SUP-9832 and linked to this thread.
Sarah O: thanks all — monitoring for another 30m. If stable we'll close this thread and start a brief postmortem. :thumbsup: :pray:
